_comment: The research tree, studied in the Scriptorium. Each branch is a short chain: a node needs the one before it (needs), sometimes a Scriptorium level (scriptorium), and for chapter branches a point in the story (when: Story.meets conditions, issue #28). cost is paid once, when you first start the node (Insight, sometimes Ink); days is study time at 100% pace (researchers' Lore speeds it up, see Empire.research_pace). effect is the one-line promise shown on the screen; the numbers themselves live in scripts/empire.gd (search for the node id) so the text and the game stay in step.

branches.name: Wardcraft
branches.blurb: Holding the line against the Blank.

branches.name: Logistics
branches.blurb: Feeding people and moving them about.

branches.name: Inkcraft
branches.blurb: What Ink can do, in the works and in a fight.

branches.name: The Abbey's Learning
branches.blurb: What the brothers of Saint Ledger's know, once they will tell you.

nodes.name: Margin Wards
nodes.effect: Every province you hold: Fray -1 a day
nodes.blurb: Little warding scribbles in the margins of every map and deed. The Blank reads the margins first, and it does not like what it finds.

nodes.name: Lampwright's Grammar
nodes.effect: Wardlamps burn brighter: Fray -1 more a day each
nodes.blurb: Lamps that are written as well as lit. The flame spells something; nobody agrees what, but the Blank flinches.

nodes.name: The Long Watch
nodes.effect: Surges are seen 1 day sooner and hit for 8 Fray, not 12
nodes.blurb: A rota of readers who stare at the edge of the white all night and write down when it twitches.

nodes.name: Ration Tables
nodes.effect: Upkeep: 1 less Supplies a day for every 4 people
nodes.blurb: Somebody finally counted the bread. Half the town had been eating twice.

nodes.name: Waystations
nodes.effect: Expeditions come back a quarter sooner
nodes.blurb: Huts, water and a dry blanket a day's walk apart. Squads stop getting lost on the way home.

nodes.name: Field Maps
nodes.blurb: Maps that are redrawn every week, because the land keeps changing its mind.

nodes.name: Spring Tapping
nodes.effect: The Inkworks makes +1 Ink a day (while it has a worker); heroes refill Ink 25% faster on missions
nodes.blurb: A better way to draw ink from the springs: slowly, and while humming. The twins insist on the humming.

nodes.name: Blotting Charm
nodes.effect: Missions: downed allies get back up 40% faster
nodes.blurb: A thumbprint of ink on the wrist. Press it to someone who has fallen and they remember they are written down.

nodes.name: Inkskin
nodes.effect: Missions: the party takes 25% less damage
nodes.blurb: Words painted on the skin under the armour. Blank teeth slide off a sentence that refuses to end.

nodes.name: Whetstones
nodes.effect: Missions: the party hits for +2 damage
nodes.blurb: Proper stones, proper oil, and a lecture on angles. Blades stop bouncing off things.

nodes.name: Boiled Leather
nodes.effect: Missions: the party starts with +10 max HP
nodes.blurb: Smells terrible, stops a bite. Everyone gets a jerkin whether they want one or not.

nodes.name: Inked Steel
nodes.effect: Missions: +3 more damage and the attack gauge refills 20% faster
nodes.blurb: Steel quenched in ink instead of water. It comes out black and slightly too eager.

nodes.name: Bell Wards
nodes.blurb: The Abbey's bells were cast with the hours written into the bronze. Rung one at a time, the right hour at the right moment, they make the Blank lose its place.

nodes.name: The Second Copy
nodes.effect: Reclaims cost 1 less Ink and bring a province back at Fray 45, not 60
nodes.blurb: How the monks meant to write the world back if the capital's Ledger burned. It works better on land that was there yesterday.

nodes.name: The Tally of Names
nodes.effect: Every province you hold with a governor: Fray -1 a day
nodes.blurb: Sister Osyth's method: count everyone, by name, and say the number out loud each night. It is very hard to erase something that is being counted.
